question: Should OpenClaw require redacted live LiteLLM-to-Anthropic cache forwarding and cache-usage proof before merging this explicit provider-capability change?
rationale: The code and focused tests establish OpenClaw payload construction, but neither they nor the current PR evidence establish the behavior of a real LiteLLM deployment and its configured Anthropic backend.

options.title: Require live provider proof
options.body: Request redacted terminal output, proxy logs, or a reproducible live transcript that shows forwarded `cache_control` and cache creation/read usage after rebasing the head.

options.title: Accept deterministic payload proof
options.body: Merge after conflict resolution if maintainers intentionally accept the explicit opt-in behavior without proving a real LiteLLM route.

options.title: Keep the canonical bug open
options.body: Pause this branch and retain https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/37966 as the tracker until a supported LiteLLM environment can supply the evidence.

recommendation.title: Require live provider proof
recommendation.body: Request redacted terminal output, proxy logs, or a reproducible live transcript that shows forwarded `cache_control` and cache creation/read usage after rebasing the head.

likelyOwner.reason: This remaining choice is chiefly about provider-boundary proof sufficiency, an area connected to this contributor's adjacent live-provider validation work.
